physicalNotes: Radius 0.10527273 Jupiter radii from Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...687A.264B/abstract): 7,526.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00553 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 1.38885844017 d
sources.shape: Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2024): a/R* 12.75; Barkaoui et al. 2024 (2024A&A...687A.264B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BARKAOUI_ET_AL_2024): inclination 87.3 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2458984.759725 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 30 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
